note: c50 (15 composers, 129 IMSLP pages, all judged). Floor evidence: Deezer album/track metadata (label, year and track timings from api.deezer.com), Apple Music (first Brahms lookups; later requests were blocked), MusicBrainz, IMSLP, Wikipedia work lists, one AllMusic listing; the Naxos Music Library and Presto were not used. The eight pages skipped for lack of a commercial recording (Fuchs Op. 61 and Op. 15, Reger's three early pieces, Lalo's Grand Quintette, Bonis's Chant nuptial, Sinding's Quartet Op. 70) were searched on Deezer and MusicBrainz and, where noted, the web; the Apple Music queue stayed blocked, so they may deserve a second look. GAP WORKS added (imslpPage null, none of them on IMSLP; Strauss's sextet is the opening of Capriccio): Bruch String Quintets in A minor and E-flat (1918) and Septet in E-flat (1849); Taneyev String Trio in B minor; Stenhammar Allegro brillante and Allegro ma non tanto; Sibelius Piano Quintet JS 159, Piano Quartets JS 157 and JS 156, String Quartets JS 184, JS 183 and Op. 4, Piano Trios JS 207 and JS 208, Suite JS 186, Harmonium Quartet JS 158; Strauss Piano Trios TrV 53 and TrV 71, Capriccio Sextet; Bonis Piano Quartet No. 1; Hahn String Quartet No. 2, Piano Quartet No. 3. NOT ADDED (not found on disc): Bruch's juvenile String Quartets (1850, 1852); Fuchs Terzetto in C-sharp minor Op. 107 (on Wikipedia's list, no IMSLP page or recording found); Bonis Fantaisie en septuor Op. 72, Suite dans le style ancien Op. 127 No. 1 and Nocturne (violin, viola, cello, harp), Hahn Piano Trio in F minor and Romance for flute and string trio; Sibelius Trio in G JS 205 and the A-minor piano trio JS 206. DECISIONS for the owner: (1) Tchaikovsky's seven 1863-64 student exercises (TH 152-159) are skipped as pedagogical, although three string-quartet pieces are recorded as "Three Short Pieces" (Moscow String Quartet, Russian Season). (2) Brahms's Piano Trio in A major (Anh. 4/5) is kept as a doubtful work because it is recorded under his name (Perlman, Mirecourt Trio, Vienna Piano Trio). (3) Taneyev's Canzona is skipped (the only recording is with string orchestra: string-orchestra question). (4) Stenhammar's withdrawn F-minor Quartet, Grieg's unfinished String Quartet No. 2 (completed by Röntgen) and Sibelius's one-movement Piano Quartet JS 156 are kept because they are recorded as they stand. (5) The viola alternative of Op. 114 is confirmed by Wikipedia (title page); that of Op. 115 rests on IMSLP's alternative title. (6) The violin list's Fuchs Op. 55 and Op. 105 and Reger Op. 131b are duos for two violins (2 players), so they stay in the violin section; Sinding's Serenades Op. 56 and 92 (two violins and piano) are cross-listed.
